Jones County article: 'Eagle Rock Partners and the engineering firm Thomas & Hutton filed to rezone more than 600 acres at Highway 18 and Bethlehem Church Road for the Crooked Creek Technology Park ... on October 20 ... the developers withdrew'. Keep ft-212 (corrected to 'withdrawn' in this file).

ft-184.name: T5 Palmetto (Palmetto Tyrone Rd)
ft-184.why: The name was just 'T5' and the developer blank. A bare 'T5' name is what let the old page mapping print this Georgia record on the Alameda, Los Angeles and El Paso County pages. The record's own source is DCD's 'T5 requests permission for 3 million sq ft campus outside Atlanta, Georgia', and the address is Palmetto Tyrone Rd, Palmetto. The Coweta County article does not mention it, so status is left. Note for the merge: T5 Fairburn (Atlanta) (t5-t5-fairburn-atlanta) is also in Palmetto, on Gullatt Rd; it may or may not be the same campus.

ft-1771618149523-4077.why: The developer field was blank. Honolulu County article: 'The one on this page is Servpac's MTP Data Center in Mililani Technology Park ... In February 2026 the locally owned company broke ground on a second building'. 'Operating (expanding)' agrees and is kept.

ft-1767322980321-2337.why: Effingham County article: 'Gail Technology ... has begun building a data center and solar array on leased farmland at 15244 E. 1700th Avenue' (this record's address). Building has begun, so 'under construction', not 'proposed'.

ft-265.why: Marion County article: 'DC Blox in Warren Township, Metrobloks in Martindale-Brightwood and Sabey in Decatur Township were already approved and are exempt' from the moratorium. The page says approved and reports no construction, and the record's own DCD source is headlined '$500m data center approved for construction'. 'Under construction' overstates what is on record.

ft-1782766364343-7627.why: The developer field reads 'Venerly LLC?', a guess with a question mark printed to the public. The record's own source is headlined 'Mystery tech firm looks to build 800-acre data center campus outside Grand Rapids', and the Kent County article names no developer for a Cedar Springs/Solon site. The developer is unknown, so null.

ft-1776036204429-9677.why: Jefferson County (MO) article: the Festus council 'annexed about 240 acres on November 10, and on November 24 rezoned about 370 acres', and on March 30, 2026 'voted 6-2 for a development agreement' with CRG; Clayco says the approval gave CRG vested rights, but 'CRG had filed no construction or permit requests as of June'. Approved, not merely proposed; lawsuit pending.

ft-343.why: Mecklenburg County article: 'In Matthews, developers of "Project Accelerate," five two-story buildings on 123 acres off East John Street that could have drawn up to 600 MW, withdrew their rezoning request on Oct. 7, 2025, days before a vote.' The developer withdrew, so 'withdrawn' rather than 'cancelled'. 600 MW is the article's stated size.

ft-359.name: Comcast Data Center (Clinton)
ft-359.why: Hunterdon County article: 'Comcast Cable is converting a vacant former TD Bank branch at 92 W. Main Street in the Town of Clinton ... the Clinton Town land use board had approved the conversion.' Approved, not proposed. Two records share the name 'Comcast Data Center' (this one and ft-361 in Moorestown), which is why this Clinton record is also printed on the Burlington County page; a distinct name fixes that. The developer was blank.

ft-323.why: The developer field was blank; the record's own name is 'Netrality Data Centers St. Louis- 210 North Tucker'. The St. Louis article does not address this building, so status is left.

ft-1768453625879-6878.why: The developer field was blank. Erie County article: 'Tesla had planned a $500 million Dojo supercomputer at its RiverBend plant on South Park Avenue in Buffalo; the Buffalo News reported Tesla has since scrapped the Dojo effort'. 'Cancelled' agrees.

ft-430.name: TierPoint Tulsa (State Farm Blvd)
ft-430.why: Two records share the exact name 'Tierpoint Data Center' (this one in Tulsa and ft-324 in St. Louis), so this Tulsa record is also printed on the St. Louis page. A distinct name separates them. The developer was blank; the record's own source is DCD's 'TierPoint completes fourth data center in Oklahoma'. The Tulsa County article does not address this building, so status is left.

ft-1776918405079-1325.why: Lackawanna County article: proposals include one in 'Newton Township, where Popca LLC applied in January 2026 for two buildings on about 90 acres and was turned down by the zoning officer.' This record is at Newton Rd, Clarks Summit (Newton Township), and its own source is WVIA's 'Proposed Newton data center campus is 10th planned for Lackawanna County'. Turned down means blocked, not proposed. The developer was blank.

ft-1770305022079-6376.name: Penn Forest Township Data Center (Maury Rd)
ft-1770305022079-6376.why: Carbon County article: 'Mele Brothers Realty of Glenside, which paid more than $2 million for land near Route 903 and Maury Road', in Penn Forest Township, where 'No developer has yet filed a plan'. The site is in Penn Forest Township (Jim Thorpe is only the postal town), so the name 'Jim Thorpe Data Center' misleads, especially as Jim Thorpe borough is separately writing its own ordinance on the same page. The developer was blank, and the ZIP was truncated to '8229' (it is 18229). Status 'proposed' is kept.

ft-1769139372684-6188.why: The record's own source is headlined (DCD URL) 'zoning-amendment-rejected-for-data-center-in-ransom-township-pennsylvania'. A rejected zoning amendment is a block, not a suspension. The Lackawanna County article lists Ransom Township among the proposals but gives no detail that contradicts this.

ft-1775616979269-7668.why: Marion County (SC) article: 'In June 2026 Stream withdrew, saying "utility power cannot be sourced on this site within the required timeframe."' The developer withdrew, so 'withdrawn' rather than 'cancelled'. The article adds that it is not reported whether the county's incentive agreement has been rescinded.

ft-527.why: The developer field was blank while the name is 'Cawley Partners' and the only source is DCD's 'Cawley Partners acquires 5,200 acres outside Dallas, plans data center park'. The Ellis County article does not mention it, so status is left.

ft-550.why: The developer field was blank, so the Collin County table prints 'Not reported' for a row named 'Experian McKinney Data Center'. The record's own sources (a TCEQ dataset and a news story on Experian's 'high-tech underground bunker') identify the operator. The Collin article does not address status.

ft-628.why: Millard County article: the Creekstone campus is 'the Delta Gigasite', 'nearly 1,200 acres southeast of the city', which Fibernet MercuryDelta asked to rezone; record ft-629 'Fibernet MercuryDelta Campus/Delta Gigasite' (developer Creekstone Energy) is that campus. This record repeats the Gigasite but carries the wrong address: '11000 McCornick Rd' is, per the same article, Joule Capital Partners' Triple C Farms site ('about 4,000 acres of the Triple C Farms at 11000 N. McCornick Road'), which has its own record (ft-1775655378279-3568). Keep ft-629; this row double-counts Creekstone at Joule's location.

ft-645.why: The record's own source is WRIC's 'Tract withdraws data center application after Chesterfield recommends against it'. The developer withdrew, so 'withdrawn' rather than 'suspended'. The developer field was blank; the name and source say Tract. The Chesterfield County article says the board has 'no appetite' for more data centers, which agrees.

ft-1047.why: Surry County article: 'on Feb. 8, 2024 supervisors approved it 3-2', then 'Green Energy Partners filed for Chapter 11 on Sept. 29, 2024' and the land purchase 'had not been completed'; the county says 'from a zoning standpoint, this private project may proceed', and 'no construction or tenant was reported'. Rezoned and approved, with nothing built and the developer in reorganization. 'Approved' is the accurate stage; 'proposed' understates the approval.

ft-1079.why: The record has no source at all. The Snohomish County article says the county has 'only one small data center on record, a Ziply Fiber facility near Paine Field drawing about 1.1 megawatts'. That contradicts an operating 'Csquare Seattle Data Center' in Lynnwood, which is in Snohomish County. With no source and the page saying otherwise, 'operating' cannot be supported.

ft-1107.why: Cabell County article: 'nothing has been reported about it since it was announced' in October 2024; work 'was to start that November', and 'Whether the first phase opened in March 2025 ... [has] not been reported'. Nothing confirms construction, so 'under construction' is unsupported. The developer was blank; the article names Doug Tate's Alpha Technologies, since rebranded Alpha Innovations.
